title: warpgate-rs/Cargo.toml
detail: Create the workspace root Cargo.toml for warpgate-rs at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\Cargo.toml. It must be a cargo workspace with resolver = "2" and members for: crates/wg-core, crates/wg-config, crates/wg-store, crates/wg-socks, crates/wg-tunnel, crates/wg-pool, crates/wg-apiserver, crates/wg-bin. title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-config
detail: Port the WarpGate config layer to Rust as crate wg-config at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-config. The reference implementation is C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\appconfig\config.go (167 lines) and the authoritative field list is C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\config.json. Requirements: a Config struct whose serde field names match config.json keys EXACTLY (snake_case as they appear in the JSON: port, max_containers, resident_count, sticky_minutes, auto_rebuild_on_unhealthy, health_check_interval, bind_address, mode, base_port, max_instances, min_available, max_concurrent_create, ip_check_url, ip_check_url_v6, openai_check_url, ip_check_retries, ip_check_interval, max_rebuild_attempts, cleanup_on_exit, rate_limit_enabled, rate_limit_per_minute, auto_rotate_on_high_403, cf_403_threshold, cf_min_check_count, ip_risk_check, ip_risk_threshold, ip_risk_ttl, ip_risk_check_url, warp_transport, log_level, public_ip, session_cleanup_interval, team_token, proxy_auth_enabled, proxy_username, proxy_password, ip_whitelist, whitelist_port_offset, api_key, masque_http2, masque_endpoint_v4, masque_endpoint_h2_v4, masque_endpoint_candidates). Provide Default::default() matching the Go defaults. Provide load(path) and validate(). Validate must reject warp_transport != "masque" with a clear error (the Go version does the same). Provide instances_dir_resolved(flag_val) following the priority --instances > WARP_INSTANCES_DIR env > config.instances_dir > ./instances. Add unit tests asserting the defaults and that C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\config.json parses successfully.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-store
detail: Port the instance-directory persistence layer to Rust as crate wg-store at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-store. Reference: C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\store\store.go (71 lines). Requirements: a Meta struct matching the Go Meta JSON tags exactly (index, name, pid, engine_pid, transport, endpoint, ipv6, status, created_at, dedicated, dedicated_remark, engine) and a UsqueConfig struct matching private_key, endpoint_v4, endpoint_v6, endpoint_h2_v4, endpoint_h2_v6, endpoint_pub_key, id, access_token, ipv4, ipv6. Functions: dir(base, index) -> base/warp-<index>, name(index) -> warp-<index>, exists(base, index), read_meta(dir), write_meta(dir, meta) with 2-space indent JSON, usque_conf_path(dir) -> dir/usque.json, read_usque_conf(path), save_usque_conf(path, cfg) with 0600 perms, remove(dir). CRITICAL: the JSON must be byte-compatible so a Go-written instances/ directory can be read by Rust and vice versa. Add a round-trip test and a test that reads a Meta with Go-style field ordering.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-core
detail: Create the shared types crate wg-core at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-core. It holds the wire-contract types shared by the other crates. Requirements: an InstanceStatus enum/consts mirroring the Go strings creating/running/unhealthy/stopped/error (use const &str so serde emits the same strings); a SwarmError-like error enum with NotFound/Conflict/Invalid/Store variants and an http_status() method returning 404/409/400/500; a Result<T> alias; the error code constants from server.js ERROR_CODES (00000 OK, A0001 UNAUTHORIZED, A0002 RATE_LIMITED, P0001 NO_AVAILABLE_PROXY, S0001 SESSION_NOT_FOUND, I0001 INVALID_INPUT, I0002 NOT_FOUND, D0001 DEDICATED_BOUND, R0001 INSTANCE_ERROR, R0002 IP_CHECK_FAILED, 99999 INTERNAL_ERROR); and the API response envelope helpers success(data) -> {code:"00000",msg:"",data} and error(code,msg,http) -> {code,msg,data:null} matching server.js L206-216. Add tests asserting the envelope JSON shape byte-for-byte.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-socks
detail: Port the SOCKS5 frontend to Rust as crate wg-socks at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-socks. Reference: C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\socks\socks5.go (287 lines) and its test socks5_test.go. Requirements: async tokio-based SOCKS5 TCP CONNECT server; method negotiation supporting NO-AUTH (0x00) and USERNAME/PASSWORD (0x02), replying 0xFF when neither is acceptable; CONNECT command only, replying 0x07 command-not-supported for BIND and UDP ASSOCIATE (must be an explicit rejection, not a silent drop); ATYP handling for IPv4 (0x01), DOMAIN (0x03) and IPv6 (0x04); a DialFunc trait for the outbound so tests can inject a fake; optional source-IP whitelist matching (entries may be bare IPs or CIDRs, empty list = port not opened); per-connection idle timeout. The domain target must be resolved locally with AAAA preferred (falling back to A) to match the Node sing-box resolve strategy prefer_ipv6. Add a test suite mirroring socks5_test.go: NO-AUTH, correct creds, wrong creds, unsupported command, whitelist reject.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-tunnel
detail: Port the MASQUE tunnel layer to Rust as crate wg-tunnel at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-tunnel. Reference: C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\wgtunnel\ (usqueconf.go 104 lines, tunnel.go 195 lines, register.go 121 lines). Requirements: a UsqueConfig type re-exported or mirrored from wg-store with EC private key parsing (base64 SEC1 DER) and endpoint public key parsing (PEM PKIX); a Tunnel struct wrapping the MASQUE connection with Start/Restart/Stop/DialContext and a status enum starting/running/reconnecting/stopped; a DialFunc override hook so offline tests can substitute the real MASQUE dial (the Go version has SetDialOverride for exactly this); the QUIC config parameters copied from Go quicConfig (KeepAlivePeriod, InitialConnectionReceiveWindow 10_000_000, MaxConnectionReceiveWindow 10_000_000, InitialStreamReceiveWindow 1_000_000, MaxStreamReceiveWindow 1_000_000, MaxIncomingStreams 100, MaxIncomingUniStreams 100); a local DNS resolver preferring AAAA then A. IMPORTANT: the actual MASQUE client (quinn + CONNECT-IP) is a Phase-3 item; for now implement the trait boundary, the config handling and the dial override, and leave the real QUIC dial behind the same trait so it can be filled in later without touching callers. Add tests for config parsing, endpoint selection (bare IP, [v6], ip:port, [v6]:port) and the dial override.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-pool
detail: Port the instance pool and scheduler to Rust as crate wg-pool at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-pool. Reference: C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\pool\manager.go (706 lines) and its three test files. Requirements: an Instance struct and a Manager owning a DashMap-like concurrent map of instances; lifecycle operations create/rebuild/stop/start/delete/rotate; cold create = register WARP account + write usque.json + start tunnel + IPv6 uniqueness check + write meta.json; warm start = reuse existing usque.json; rebuild = delete dir and recreate at the same index with max_rebuild_attempts; rotate = delete account and re-register for a new exit IPv6; crash self-heal with exponential backoff 1s->2s->4s capped at 60s and unhealthy marking after the threshold; max_concurrent_create enforced with a tokio Semaphore; resident_count and max_instances honoured. Scheduler: Round-Robin pick skipping unhealthy (but INCLUDING unknown, per the v11.0 fix); sticky sessions keyed by session_id with sticky_minutes expiry; both periodic sweep (session_cleanup_interval) and lazy deletion on acquire. The tunnel dial must be injectable so the e2e test can run offline, mirroring the Go e2e_test.go which injects a local echo server. Add tests mirroring manager_test.go and an offline e2e test mirroring e2e_test.go.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-apiserver
detail: Port the HTTP management API to Rust as crate wg-apiserver at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-apiserver. Reference: C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\internal\apiserver\server.go (658 lines) and server_test.go. Requirements: axum router covering ALL the routes server.js exposes (68 route registrations) including /api/login, /api/check, /api/containers, /api/stats, /api/create, /api/delete, /api/rebuild, /api/start, /api/stop, /api/job/:id, /api/whitelist, /api/creds/set, /api/config, /api/pool/acquire, /api/proxies, /api/usage, /api/pool/release, /api/pool/report, /api/pool/status, /api/pool/rotate, /api/pool/dedicated/bind, /api/pool/dedicated/unbind, /api/pool/dedicated, /api/pool/dedicated/remark, /api/pool/dedicated/history, /api/creds/reset, /api/key, /api/key/reset. Auth must match the Go semantics: X-API-Key header, Authorization Bearer, and ?key= query param; whitelisted or loopback source IPs bypass the key; a login token signed with HMAC over api_key; 5 failed logins lock for 60s. Responses must use the wg-core envelope. Static pages (/, /docs, /key) are served from a public dir resolved via WARP_PUBLIC_DIR. Rate limiting on the /api/pool and mutation routes per rate_limit_per_minute. Add tests mirroring server_test.go.

title: warpgate-rs/crates/wg-bin
detail: Create the binary crate wg-bin at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\crates\wg-bin that wires everything together, mirroring C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-go\main.go (64 lines). Requirements: clap-based flags --config (default config.json), --instances, --version; load config via wg-config; init tracing from log_level; warn and continue when masque_http2 is true because the embedded L4Proxy only speaks QUIC/UDP (the Go main.go does exactly this); create the instances dir; construct the pool Manager; call Boot (recover existing instances then create up to resident_count); call StartLoops (sticky cleanup + health check); start the axum server on bind_address:port; handle SIGINT/SIGTERM with a graceful shutdown that gives in-flight work 5 seconds. Add a Dockerfile at C:\Users\zs\Desktop\WarpGate2\warpgate-rs\Dockerfile using a distroless or scratch static build with the public/ assets copied in, plus a README describing build and run.
